candidate.derivedAnswer: y decreases as x increases; the graph passes through quadrants I, II, and IV.
candidate.answerReason: The coefficient -3 is negative, so the function decreases. For x<0, y>0; for 0<x<1/3, y>0; and for x>1/3, y<0. These give quadrants II, I, and IV, respectively.

methods.label: Use the signs of k and b
methods.explanation: \(k=-3<0\), so \(y\) decreases as \(x\) increases. Since \(b=1>0\), the graph intersects the positive \(y\)-axis. Combined with \(k<0\), this shows that the graph passes through the first, second, and fourth quadrants.
methods.levelReason: Directly applies the Grade 8 properties of a linear function.
